banner.title: TABLE 50 (HAND HELD WEAPONS, GENERAL DATA AND TO HIT ADJUSTMENTS), printed capture p. 80 - the OA hand-held weapons round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture (the settling authority), with the cross-capture check available for the first time above p. 33: the compressed-print capture OCR'd full this turn gives a second independent read of the page - the 49-row grid cross-checked cell-by-cell between the two passes; four cells contest and all settle per the print capture (the katana AC-8, sword-short AC-8 and tui-fa AC-9 cells read +1 in the print against the compressed -1, a non-monotonic dip that contradicts its own ladder - the R622 doctrine kills the compressed class; the jo-stick AC-5 cell reads -1 in the print against the compressed -2 - both ladder-consistent, the settling print read stands, the cell flags for the physical-copy check). T50 pins as the 49-row hand-held grid: the speed factor bounds (the lone numbers as lo=hi; the chijiriki-spear, spear and trident 6-8 and the whip 5-8 as printed ranges), the eleven-column AC 0-10 to-hit adjustment ladder, the footnote letters as the R640 bitmask (the mace h 128, the tetsu-bishi d 8), and the chijiriki-chain row - its printed dashes pin as -99 and its (see chain) cross-reference pins as a bool; the length and space-required columns are textual and ride the column comments per the T48 doctrine. The footnote texts are not re-pinned: the block printed under T50 serves both tables and was pinned in R640; the d and h lines reprint under the T50 tail serving the two marker rows. OCR normalizations: the names and lengths pin as printed (the kawanga spelling per the R640 settle; the compressed pass's 2* tetsu-bishi length reads as 2'; the plus-after-prime cells print as N + and pin as printed; the half-foot glyph rides the comment). The weapons descriptions prose box stays open; Table 51 (capture pp. 80-81) is deliberately left for the next round
